name: new_pillar_type
title: Prepare a column type for formatting

origin.description: Look up the short type name and prepare the label format() draws under the title.

arguments.name: x
arguments.text: A vector whose type is retrieved with type_sum().
Further arguments must be empty. A value here warns, and the type is still built.

origin.details: type_sum() of a character vector is chr, and of a factor is fct. format_type_sum() wraps that name in angle brackets and paints it subtle and italic. The object's width is the display width of that label, and at least 5. The minimum width is 5. The label does not depend on the values, so letters and the string "a" are the same type.

translation.description: The same label. A factor is Factor. None is not a factor.

arguments.name: x
arguments.text: A vector, a string, or a Factor. type_sum supplies the short name. A character value is chr. Factor(["a"]) is fct.

translation.details: format() calls format_type_sum. With 8 colors the label is italic, then grey, then the brackets, then the two closes. The width is the display width of that string, and at least 5, so chr and fct are both width 5. The minimum width stays 5 even when the label is wider, as with a one-column data frame. A narrow width trims the name before the brackets are added. is_focus underlines the whole label. An unexpected keyword is an error with the check_dots_empty text.
translation.value: A pillar_type. format() returns one styled string.
translation.example:
from cli._options import options as cli_options

cli_options(**{"cli.num_colors": 8, "cli.unicode": True})

from pillar._vec import Factor
from pillar.parts import new_pillar_type

print(new_pillar_type("a").format())
print(new_pillar_type(Factor(["a"])).format())
